**Verdict:** Structurally and editorially strong, but a load-bearing factual claim in the title/body needs reconciliation before public publication.

**Primary blocker — dating conflicts with the documented Xultun record**
- Title says "1,300-year-old math"; body and `imageAlt` say "mid-eighth century"; lede says "roughly 1,300 years ago." The Xultun astronomical room (Structure 10K-2, Saturno et al.) is dated to the **early ninth century (~AD 813–814)**, not the mid-eighth. From 2026 that is ~1,210 years old, which rounds to **1,200**, not 1,300. As written, the headline age appears ~1 century too old.
- This is the most prominent claim on the page, so it must be corrected or explicitly reconciled against the cited Antiquity 2026 paper if that paper re-dates the text. It cannot ship unverified in the title.

**Secondary — unverifiable load-bearing specifics (confirm against sources)**
- `content:34` "over **50** mathematical and astronomical microtexts" and "**11 hieroglyphs" — precise counts with no in-text attribution; verify these come from the Antiquity/Nature sources.
- Name and gloss "**Sak Tahn Waax**, or 'White-Chested Fox'" and the "so says…" attribution — central to the piece; confirm the translation and reading match the primary source.
- I could not independently validate the four external sources (`content:80-83`), incl. DOI `10.15184/aqy.2026.10378`; these post-date my knowledge and must be confirmed live before publication given the whole story rests on them.

- Frontmatter well-formed; slug matches filename; tags/category coherent. ✓

Recommend: correct/verify the age in title, lede, body, and `imageAlt` to match the cited source, and confirm the numeric specifics and four references resolve before publishing.
